themes.label: Public-to-private buyout offers on listed companies
themes.note: Sponsors, strategics and insiders keep taking listed businesses off public markets, and the spread between what the public market pays and what private capital will pay is the whole story. The newest approach comes from a brand licensor: Authentic Brands Group has privately discussed buying Mattel at more than $20 a share, about $6bn and a 58%+ premium, with no formal sale process and a new CEO starting the same week (mat-authentic-brands-takeover-approach). Insider buyouts show the opening bid is a floor: Priority Technology's chairman and CEO Thomas Priore was pushed by a special committee to $8.05 a share, more than 30% above his opening range, backed by Searchlight Capital Partners (prth-priore-searchlight-take-private). Third-party sponsors show the full premium range: Sequence Holdings and Michael Dell's DFO Management are paying $32.50 a share for Baldwin, an 88% premium to its unaffected June price, while H.I.G. is taking MISTRAS at $20.35, just 8% over the 30-day VWAP, with a go-shop to 27 October (bwin-sequence-dfo-take-private, mg-hig-take-private). Tender mechanics are now the risk: Copart had only 47.8% of ACV Auctions tendered by 30 September against a majority minimum and has extended its $10.50 offer to 7 October after refiling its HSR notice (cprt-acv-acquisition); Uber's EUR41.50 tender for Delivery Hero runs to November (dher-uber-takeover-offer); and Curaleaf's hostile bid for Aurora Cannabis runs to 1 December against a reject recommendation and dueling Alberta Securities Commission applications (acb-curaleaf-takeover-bid). Two are effectively done: L'imad will own more than 98.5% of AD Ports and delist it once settlement completes by 9 October (adports-limad-takeover-bid), and Peel declared its 187p offer for Harworth unconditional with 52% of the shares (hwg-peel-acquisition).

themes.label: AI data-center capacity and power build-out
themes.note: Capital keeps flowing to the physical layer of AI compute, and the bottleneck keeps moving down the stack to power and capacity. Getting power onto a site is the scarcest input, and Amazon has contracted the generators themselves, committing $2.4bn across 2027-28 and up to $8bn over the life of a backup-power agreement with Generac -- a company whose franchise was suburban home standby until this deal made hyperscaler capex its swing factor (gnrc-amazon-generator-supply). The pull now reaches the regulated utilities and the politics around them: NextEra's $67bn all-stock purchase of Dominion, the largest regulated utility deal ever announced, is being fought in Virginia over exactly who pays for data-center load growth, with the September concession package funding four years of residential bill credits by redirecting credits that would otherwise have gone to data centers -- a package Virginia's attorney general now argues is a new deal that should restart the 180-day review clock and push the hearing to January (nee-dominion-acquisition). The pull has also reached CDN and edge-compute providers: Anthropic will pay Akamai $11.6bn over seven years, with an option for $9bn more, for CPU-heavy cloud capacity, and Akamai is lifting 2026 capex by about $1.7bn to build it, paid for partly with a warrant over about 5% of its shares (akam-anthropic-cloud-deal).

themes.label: Signed M&A deals hitting regulatory or legal roadblocks
themes.note: Deals investors thought were settled keep being resolved by regulators, politicians and courts rather than by the parties. Paramount's $111bn purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery had cleared 68 jurisdictions and still could not close until the 12-state antitrust suit was settled on 21 September; there were no divestitures, but the price was a five-year court-enforceable behavioural package -- $1.5bn of extra domestic film spend, a 30-then-32 annual release floor with a $30m payment per film missed, a $47.5m worker fund, a five-year ban on selling the Los Angeles lots and an independent board over CBS News and CNN -- commitments that are now fixed charges on the synergy case, with closing guided to early October -- and the settlement itself is now the obstacle: at a 24 September hearing Judge Martinez-Olguin said the court 'is not a rubber stamp', admitted amicus briefs from the Block the Merger coalition, asked the parties to answer Senator Booker's objections by 28 September and deferred her ruling, and on 30 September she approved it as a 'reasonable factual and legal resolution', leaving Paramount guiding to a 6 October close (psky-wbd-acquisition). Kone's EUR29.4bn purchase of TK Elevator is the freshest version and the most exposed: the UK Competition and Markets Authority has begun canvassing third parties ahead of a phase 1 case while the US Department of Justice runs an in-depth review that can last a year or more, against a Q2 2027 completion target (knebv-tkelevator-acquisition). Uber-Delivery Hero shows how long the tail runs even when nobody is fighting: an agreed, board-recommended tender has now entered pre-merger review in Korea, where the regulator is examining common control of Uber's taxi-hailing arm and Baedal Minjok, one clearance among a 99-country footprint that pushes settlement into the second half of 2027 (dher-uber-takeover-offer). NextEra-Dominion is the unresolved US version: every economic term is agreed and both shareholder bases have voted, yet the deal turns on Virginia's State Corporation Commission, and the companies have already doubled residential bill relief and lifted the credit pool to $1.87bn to buy approval -- only for the state attorney general to argue that the concessions amount to an amended application that should reset the 180-day review clock and move the hearing to January (nee-dominion-acquisition). The counter-example is what a clean path looks like: Bio-Techne's US antitrust waiting period simply expired and its holders voted the Merck KGaA deal through, leaving only foreign clearances (tech-merckkgaa-acquisition); Iridium holders likewise voted 99.6% for Rocket Lab's cash-and-stock offer, though regulatory work still stretches the close to mid-2027 (irdm-rocketlab-acquisition). In Canada the Alberta Securities Commission has been drafted into the Curaleaf-Aurora fight by both sides (acb-curaleaf-takeover-bid). Transocean-Valaris is the latest clean exit: the DOJ closed its second-request investigation of the $5.8bn all-stock offshore-drilling merger on 30 September without remedies, leaving only Brazil before a Q4 close (val-transocean-acquisition). Even a small, uncontroversial tender can slip on process: Copart withdrew and refiled its HSR notice for ACV Auctions on 28 September, pushing the waiting period to 13 October and forcing an extension of the offer to 7 October (cprt-acv-acquisition). Onsemi's revised Synaptics deal already has FTC clearance, so the remaining risk there is the shareholder vote and the unnamed rival bidder rather than regulators (syna-onsemi-acquisition).

themes.label: Financial firms buying platforms and product lines rather than building them
themes.note: Companies keep concluding that the capabilities the market now pays for are quicker to buy than to build, and that what they are buying is a distribution platform or a fee stream rather than assets. Grab has paid $1.49bn for 60% of Atome Financial to acquire a working BNPL, cards and digital-lending platform across five Southeast Asian markets rather than originating its own book (grab-atome-acquisition). The domestic version is Aon's $17bn all-cash purchase of USI's middle-market brokerage platform from KKR, now funded with a $13.5bn seven-part bond sale that drew about $65bn of orders -- the price of buying rather than building, written onto Aon's own balance sheet (aon-usi-acquisition).

themes.label: Large-caps scaling up buybacks on surplus cash
themes.note: Six companies with cash coming in faster than they can reinvest it have expanded share repurchases in under a week, each tying the bigger programme to a specific cash or capital tailwind. Nvidia added $150bn to its authorization on 28 September -- the largest increase ever, taking remaining capacity to $235bn through fiscal 2028 -- on AI-accelerator cash flow (nvda-buyback-2026). The same day TotalEnergies lifted Q4 buybacks to $2.5bn from $1.5bn and pledged more than 5% annual dividend growth through 2030 as oil trades around $100 (tte-buyback-dividend-2026). Lear lifted its authorization to $1.5bn, about 26% of its market value, and extended it to 2029 (lea-buyback-2026). Canadian banks are moving together: on 30 September TD, days after completing a C$7bn programme, said it intends to buy back up to another C$10bn (about 3.7% of its shares) by July 2027 (td-buyback-2026), and on 2 October Scotiabank lifted its issuer bid to 40 million shares from 15 million, about 3.25% of its stock (bns-buyback-2026). Regulatory relief is the newest trigger: Julius Baer announced a CHF600m buyback the same day, days after FINMA closed its Signa probe and halved an extra capital requirement (baer-buyback-2026). The common signal is that management teams see their own stock as the best use of surplus cash rather than new capacity or M&A.
